title: Land the failed Lane 2 by fixing its two test bugs and flipping it to held
context: Lane 2 of wave 1 (streak-pill, phone-shell-chrome, macos-sidebar) finished all of its code, but the Worker reported failed. Two of its own acceptance tests had test-side bugs, and the receipts edit hook locked them after their first red run, so the Worker could not fix them. Lanes 3, 7, 8, 9 and 10 depend on Lane 2. The sidebar collapse test turns reduce motion on to stop the petals, and that makes AnimationController run 20 times faster, so its 125 ms mid-animation width check can never catch the resize in progress.
options: Re-dispatch Lane 2 with a fresh Worker (another long Opus Lane, which would re-derive the same two fixes)
Apply the handoff's two verified test fixes in the worktree, then flip Lane 2 to held in state.json so the resume lands it without re-running it
For the sidebar test, toggle reduce motion off around the tap to catch the width mid-animation, at the cost of starting the petals and making pumpAndSettle hang
For the sidebar test, assert the rail's AnimatedContainer has duration 250 ms and curve Cubic(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)
outcome: I applied the two fixes myself and will flip Lane 2 to held, so the resume lands its write-set without paying for the Lane again. For glass_toast_test, the MaterialApp in `_show` gets `key: UniqueKey()`. For sidebar_collapse_test, I chose the AnimatedContainer duration-and-curve assertion. It checks the 0.25 s resize the spec names without fighting the reduce-motion speed-up the test needs to stop the petals. Both files pass all 4 tests, and analyze is clean. The fix was made by the orchestrating session rather than a Worker, so the Lane 2 record's notes and the PR body will say so.
